answer: Admission needs 1 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. Since the lotus escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the beacon audit releases each pair. A farm running 27 keys cannot self-supply these, as each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the raven graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
